title: Switch
lead: A switch represents a physical switch that allows someone to choose between two mutually exclusive options. For example, "On/Off" and "Show/Hide". Choosing an option should produce an immediate result.

examples.name: Checked
examples.description: A Switch can be initially checked by passing a value to the `defaultChecked` property, or have its checked value controlled via the `checked` property.

examples.name: Size
examples.description: A Switch can have different sizes.

examples.name: Label
examples.description: A label can be provided to the Switch and is positioned above, before or after the component.

examples.name: Label Wrapping
examples.description: The label will wrap if it is wider than the available space. The Switch track will stay aligned to the first line of text.

examples.name: Required
examples.description: When a Switch is marked as `required`, its label also gets the required styling.

prose.text:
## Best practices

### Layout

- When people need to perform extra steps for changes to take effect, use a check box instead. For example, if they must click a "Submit", "Next", or "OK" button to apply changes, use a check box.

### Content

- Only replace the On/Off labels if there are more specific labels for the setting. For example, you might use Show/Hide if the setting is "Show images".
- Keep descriptive text short and concise—two to four words; preferably nouns. For example, "Focused inbox" or "WiFi".
